captions.instagram:
How do automatic doors work?

Open up the box above a sliding door: one belt moves two leaves in opposite directions. Walk a figure at the tiny radar that hears your footsteps as a 225 Hz hum, stop in the doorway, stand a bag in the way, cut the power, and see why the glass never shuts on you.

→ An automatic door hides its whole machine in the box above your head.
→ One belt, two leaves: one clamps to the top run, the other to the bottom, so they always move opposite ways.
→ The black box above the door is a tiny radar. Walk towards it and your echo comes back about 225 Hz higher.
→ Walk away and the echo drops instead, so a smart sensor does not hold the door open for you.
→ Radar cannot see a person standing still, so a curtain of infrared spots on the floor watches the doorway.

Play with it yourself. It's free and open source: glassbox.how/autodoorclear (link in bio)

youtubeLong.title: How do automatic doors work? (interactive explainer)
youtubeLong.description:
Open up the box above a sliding door: one belt moves two leaves in opposite directions. Walk a figure at the tiny radar that hears your footsteps as a 225 Hz hum, stop in the doorway, stand a bag in the way, cut the power, and see why the glass never shuts on you.

▶ Play with the interactive version: https://glassbox.how/e/autodoorclear/
⌘ Source code (MIT): https://github.com/bdeeps/autodoorclear

In this video:
• The machine is in the box above your head. A sliding door's leaves hang from wheeled carriages on a track in the header.
• A tiny radar hears you coming. The usual sensor is a microwave radar at about 24 GHz.
• A curtain of infrared sees you standing. Radar only detects motion, so a person who stops in the doorway disappears from it.
• Fast in the middle, gentle at the ends. The controller counts pulses from an encoder on the motor to know where the leaves are, and follows a plan: accelerate, cruise, brake, creep.
• It must never become a wall. When the mains fails, a battery opens the door and parks it.
• Other doors, other ideas. A swing-door operator opens a hinged door slowly enough to stop with one hand.

Glassbox opens one box a day: an interactive model of how something works, plus the code behind it.
